Nurses, residents and veterans' families are your neighbors and your customers. Show them a site that respects their time, and see a free demo of yours first.

Web design in Temple, TX starts with knowing who is searching. This is the Temple in Bell County, Texas, not the university in Philadelphia that shows up in the same searches. It is a medical town on I-35, and a lot of the people looking for a sitter, a lunch spot, a physical therapist or an apartment work long shifts at a hospital and have five minutes to decide. Maurice Johnson, a Texan in Big Sandy, writes those sites by hand and shows you a free demo before you pay anything.

Two hospitals, a warehouse row and a growing town

Baylor Scott & White, which the Temple Economic Development Corporation calls the largest not-for-profit health care system in Texas, has its medical center here. So does the Olin E. Teague Veterans' Medical Center, the main campus of the Central Texas Veterans Health Care System, which serves veterans across 39 Texas counties. Distribution is the other big employer: McLane Company is based in Temple, and H-E-B and Walmart run distribution centers here.

The town is growing to match. The Census Bureau put Temple at 82,073 people in 2020 and 93,095 by its July 2023 estimate, a rise of 13.4% in three years. New residents mean people choosing a dentist, a mechanic and a hair stylist for the first time, usually on a phone.

Hospital staff

Shift workers need hours that are on the page, early or late openings stated plainly, and booking that does not require a call during a twelve-hour shift.

Veterans and their families

Many come to Temple for care. They look for services near the VA campus, clear directions and someone who will explain things patiently.

Newcomers on I-35

Families moving in for new jobs search for everything at once. A site that names the neighborhoods you serve wins the first call.

Temple web design for small practices and home health

Big hospitals draw a ring of small health businesses: physical and speech therapy, counseling, home health agencies, medical equipment, chiropractors and dentists. Their websites have the same job. Say what you treat, who you see, where you are, what plans you take, and how to make the first appointment.

  • Services in plain words a patient uses, not billing codes
  • Accepted insurance listed only as you confirm it
  • A referral page for doctors' offices and case managers
  • Hours, parking and accessibility, stated up front

The trades that keep a growing town working

Every new apartment complex and subdivision means plumbing calls, air conditioning repairs and cleaning jobs. Google ranks local results on relevance, distance and prominence, so a plumber whose site clearly says it covers Temple, Belton and the neighborhoods in between gives Google, and a new homeowner, a reason to pick it. Starter at $497 covers five pages and goes live in 7 to 14 days; Pro at $997 adds ten city pages, each one researched and written fresh. We do not sell page counts.

Where Temple owners can get free help

The Temple EDC, formed in 1989, works with a network that includes the Temple Chamber of Commerce, Bell County, Temple College and the Small Business Development Center. The Chamber traces itself to a citywide commercial club formed in 1907 and has worked with neighboring chambers and SCORE on small business seminars. In Killeen, the Central Texas Business Resource Center offers counseling and training through Central Texas College, Workforce Solutions of Central Texas and the Greater Killeen Chamber.

Built for Temple from East Texas

Straight answer on location: Dominion Web Design Pro has no office in Temple. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy in East Texas and delivers it remotely, by link, phone and email.

Send your practice or business name and the services you want patients and customers to find. The preview is free.

Common questions

Is this temple web design page about Temple University?

No. This page is about Temple, Texas, the city in Bell County on I-35 between Waco and Austin. If you were looking for web design classes or projects at Temple University in Philadelphia, this is not that. If you run a business in Temple, Texas, you are in the right place.

How much does web design cost for a small practice in Temple, TX?

Our packages are paid once: Starter is $497 for five hand-written pages, Pro is $997 for ten pages plus local SEO and ten researched city pages, and Agency is $1,997. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep an AI agent. A solo therapist or a small home health agency usually starts with Starter or Pro.

Can my website mention which insurance plans or VA programs we accept?

Yes, and it should if it is true. Patients in Temple often ask which plans you take before anything else. List only what you actually accept, keep it current, and give a phone number for questions. Maurice writes what you confirm and nothing more.

Do you meet Temple business owners in person?

No. Maurice Johnson works from Big Sandy in East Texas and handles every project by phone, email and shared links. Call (903) 636-7511 any hour; an AI receptionist answers and can put you through to Maurice.

See a Temple website built for your business

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
